Adjusted interpretation using SLOOS context:
- The FOMC’s 75 bp hike to 3–3.25%, guidance for “ongoing increases,” and continued balance sheet runoff remain distinctly hawkish.
- July 2022 SLOOS indicates a pronounced tightening in bank lending standards and terms across C&I (for firms of all sizes) and CRE, with banks increasing loan spreads, collateral requirements, and costs. Banks cited a weaker/more uncertain economic outlook and reduced risk tolerance as key reasons. Residential real estate and consumer credit also saw tighter standards, including for credit cards and auto loans. Demand was mixed: stronger for C&I and HELOCs but weaker in CRE and parts of RRE.
- This SLOOS evidence implies the credit channel is tightening alongside policy, amplifying restrictive financial conditions and downside risks to growth beyond the baseline hawkish read. While robust employment provides some cushion, tighter bank lending points to more drag ahead.

Net: More risk-off than the FSR-only assessment; downgrade sentiment modestly further.
